answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent's history to a succinct Merkle root and verifiable delay primitives force any challenger to perform sequential work. Staking collateral equal to maximal reputation incurs slashing penalties on double-signing, yielding negative expected attack utility. The protocol reaches a robust Nash equilibrium as the zephyr of entropy, the gale of adversarial pressure, and the tide of cryptographic finality make identity cloning computationally infeasible.
